studies.headline: Tringa glareola occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.

studies.detail: Occupancy 0.782 in 1987-1991 against 0.703 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.125 and 0.084.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

studies.detail: Occupancy 0.284 in 1987-1991 against 0.204 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.010 and 0.011.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

rows.label: Reporting rate, uncorrected
rows.detail: 0.157 to 0.113 — the share of cells the bird was seen in at all, which is what the answer would have been without a detection model

rows.label: Against the other five-year window
rows.detail: 2019-2023 in place of 2008-2012, and the sign agrees

studies.headline: Acroteriobatus annulatus is recorded here, and nothing here measures it.

studies.caveat: Absence of a result is not a result. This says the data cannot answer the question, not that the answer is no.
